properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.62(a)13 - DISPOSAL OF RESIDUAL WASTE - PITS - Owner or operator failed to inspect liner for lack of uniformity, damage and other imperfections that may cause the liner to leak and repair damages to pit liner prior to placing waste in the pit.
Violation ID: 950891
Permit API: 129-26012
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Rostraver Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 4/07/2022
Comments: This admin inspection is being conducted in response to review of 3rd party consultant, Moody and Associates, Inc., investigation report for the Manack 2 Well Site in Rostraver Township, Westmoreland County. Review of DEP inspections, Moody's investigation report and ES plans for the well site were conducted. In IR 3011479 and IR 3310984, drill cutting pit locations and waste manifests were requested and were unable to be obtained, due to the well site transfer from Atlas Resources to Diversified Oil and Gas. Diversified OG suspected the drill cuttings were land farmed which corroborated with the well site's ES plan. However, in Moody's report, they identified the approximate locations of the cuttings pit by increasing the the vertical exaggeration of the terrain in Good Earth and confirming with land owner upon a site visit conducted March 19th, 2020. The drill pit was located approximately 50 ft northwest of the well. Results reported by DEP and Moody's indicated elevated metal concentrations and pH levels in several locations around the well site. Due to reported lab results and identification of drill pit by Moody, the Department recommends that the Operator evaluate the integrity of the drill pit. Based on DEP sample results and Moody's investigation report, violations are being issued under 78.61 and 78.62.

Comments: On May 17, 2022, I conducted an inspection of the Ziolkowski 11771 Well Site in Findlay Township, Allegheny County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 5/17/2022 at 12:23am. According to the report at 11:15pm, a water hauler released approximately 40 barrels of brine water to the well pad and access road. During the inspection, I observed staining along the east side of Potato Garden Road leading from the well site access road heading north toward State Route 30. I was accompanied by RRC representative Nate Smiell. The Act 9 sign was installed. The PPC plan and ER plan were on site I observed staining on the north side of the access road from the wells site entrance up to the well pad. The staining appeared to be approximately 4’ to 6’ in width, the impacted depth was estimated to be between 2" and 6" deep depending on the specific location. The Operator was in the process of scraping the stained material from the access road with a small bulldozer and loading roll off boxes with a skid steer. The Operator had progressed from the well site entrance up the access road approximately 400’. The Operator excavated the impacted material from the well pad and placed the material in roll off disposal boxes. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 480’ in length, 35’ wide with a depth of 4" to 6". The total length of the impacted area at the location (well and access road) is approximately 1,700’, with varying widths and depths. The release did not appear to reach waters of the commonwealth from the well site or access road and did not appear to impact the PCSM basins on site. The release appeared to be contained to the well pad, access road and sections the channel adjacent to the access road. Violation are being issued for the release of a regulated fluid. I recommend that the Operator continue to follow the Departments most recent spill policy for remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/25/2026 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Pike Township, Bradford county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8268725
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On 03/24/2026 at 1132 hours Repsol reported (CTS#396090) that at 0600 hours they noticed fluid in the southside ditch of the Ugliuzza well pad that was going towards the catch basin. There was a hose that did not have a cap on it and the fluid was coming from the hose. They are estimating ~630 gallons (1 barrel=42 gallons) of produced water was released off containment. Resource Management was contracted to conduct remediation. At ~1525 hours Repsol contacted the DEP to update the amount release to be ~18,900 gallons. Four water trucks off-loading onsite each contained 4,620 gallons of produced fluid. It is estimated that the release traveled 1,143 feet downhill to the stream. A remediation plan is in place, and they are implementing it as we spoke. On 03/23/2026 at 2218 hours the first of five water trucks arrived onsite to off-load fluid for upcoming completion activities. From 2218-0319 hours 4 water trucks off-loaded onsite. At 0615 hours on 03/24/2026 a 5th water truck started offloading and immediately noticed the leak and stopped off-loading. On 03/25/2026 Repsol reported that as of 0700 hours ~10,500 gallons of fluid had been recovered from the stormwater channel and basin. On 03/25/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection report of Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad. Water Quality Specialists Korey Starkey, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived at ~ 0930 hours. Licensed Professional Geologist Samuel Louderback arrived at approximately 1100 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Meagan DePue and Resource Management. Fenton Excavation was onsite excavating within the LOD to capture fluids during the inspection. Meagan stated that she contacted the PFBC and left a message. She informed us that a hose connected to the manifold was not connected to the produced fluid tanks and that it was hanging over the side of the secondary containment into the stormwater ditch while the first four trucks off-loaded (photo #2-6). The produced fluid then flowed to the stormwater basin (photo #7) and through the drainage pipe of the stormwater basin (photo #9) into a natural conveyance channel which reached a UNT to Rockwell Creek. The DEP, Repsol and Resource Management walked the impacted area together. Resource Management set up monitoring points and split sampled during that time. The fluids in the stormwater ditch were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~7.85 mS/cm. There was a sump pump in the stormwater ditch (photo #5). A sample was collected from the stormwater basin at 1204 hours (photo #8). The EC of the sampled fluids were >19.99 mS/cm. Fluids were able to escape the basin through an outflow pipe. Two sumps were constructed inside and outside of the basin (photo #7 and 10). Fluids collected in the sumps were being actively recovered.The EC of the drainage area beyond the stormwater basin was ~1.8 mS/cm and the soil EC was ~4.8 mS/cm (photo #11). The drainage area forms a conveyance channel ~500ft down from the release location. The EC of the conveyance channel was ~5.4 mS/cm (photo #12). There was a spring adding water to the channel ~900ft downstream from the release location. It was located above grade (photo #13). The EC of the spring was ~100 us/cm. We traveled ~500ft downstream the conveyance channel and obtained EC readings between 2.6-2.7 mS/cm (photo #14 and 15).We traveled downstream ~435ft. The conveyance channel EC was between 5.8-8.0 mS/cm (photo #16 and 17). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1053 hours from the UNT upstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #18). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1118 hours from the UNT downstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #22).The EC of Rockwell Creek ~1.4 miles away was ~0.15 mS/cm.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 6/04/2024
Comments: On June 4th, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/4/24 at 12:04 PM (CTS 381210). Present at today's inspection is William Warfel of Diversified Energy.At the time of this inspection, William stated that at 10:30 AM on 6/4/24 while onsite at the Davenport well, they had noticed some staining on the gravel underneath the production tank valve and a large patch of dead vegetation downslope of the well site. After using measuring devices to gauge the fluid level in the production tank, it was determined that approximately 18-20 barrels had released from the production tank. William stated that prior to the Department arriving onsite, a water truck had already come and emptied the remainder of the production tank. The production tank once empty, was then moved adjacent to where it once sat so that removal of contaminated material could begin. William showed the Department a small area on the valve pipe of the production tank where they believe the leak came from. The Department observed a dried white chalky substance on this area of the valve pipe presumed to be dried brine water. William hypothesizes that the brine water travel down the shale bank adjacent to where the production tank used to sit and pooled in the once grassy lot downslope of the well site.Upon observation of the area downslope of the production tank, the Department noticed an approximately 15ft by 8ft area of dead vegetation and mud with sheeny/iridescent puddles throughout. The Department then took a soil conductivity reading upslope of the production tank in some vegetation adjacent to the well site as a background (0.1337 mS), another in the stained gravel underneath where the production tank valve hole was (1.35 mS), and then on the shale hill leading down to the now dead vegetation adjacent to well site (1.454 mS). Then the Department began taking soil conductivity readings at the bottom of this hill to gauge how wide of an area the spill impacted. A soil conductivity reading was taken in a sheeny/iridescent puddle observed in some mud that was surrounded by dead vegetation (Over range), it was evident that all areas lacking vegetation and that were visibly wet and iridescent were impacted, so the Department went to the edge of this area to determine if any vegetated areas were impacted as well. The dead vegetation looks to be a pathway of where the release may have traveled and it leads right up to a small wooded area. Soil conductivty readings were taken at the edge of the dead vegetation where it meets the wooded area (7.63mS), another taken adjacent to the previous reading in a spot that is also where the dead vegetation meets the woods (5.51 mS), in the wooden area about 1 foot from the dead vegetation (4.90 mS) and even further in the wooded area, about 3 feet in from the dead vegetation (0.1747 mS). A reading was also taken in the grass to the left of the dead vegetation (0.280 mS) to see if that grassy area was impacted as well. These soil conductivity readings subjugate that the impacted area goes beyond where you can visibly see puddles and dead vegetation. While onsite the Department let William know that areas outside of the dead vegetation area are elevated and recommended that when removing contaminated material they give themselves a buffer area larger than 3 feet in each direction. William stated that Spartan Specialty Services would be onsite soon to place impacted soil and gravel into dumpsters and that details will be provided in the Act 2 summary report. William stated that silt fences will also be installed to ensure there are not any erosion and sedimentation issues during the removal process.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for this 18-20 barrel release of brine fluid onto the gravel well site and the adjacent grass lot and wooded area.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). SPSI began excavating a pothole, approx. 3 ft in depth; pooled fluid observed within. Conductivity reading within excavated hole was 6.30 mS. Vegetated berm adjacent to hole, above impacted area, displayed a reading of 0.34 mS (18-20). Additional readings within vegetation beyond western edge of impacted area displayed 2.21-6.44 mS (21-23). Reading in fluid contained within secondary containment around ASTs w/ level of 7.20 mS. Due to observed release of production fluid within vegetation on site and potential for fluid to impact WOC downslope of impacted area, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued. Additional violations of 78a.66(b)(2) for failure to report within 2 hours, 78a.66(b)1(i), 78a.66(b)1(ii), and 91.33(a) for threatening WOC pollution, 5 gallons not completely contained and failure to report to DEP and downstream users are being issued. Additional follow up inspections to be conducted to monitor WOC downslope of impacted area.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8162072
Permit API: 123-45892
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Glade Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/10/2023
Comments: On 10/10/2023, I conducted an inspection due to an incident that occurred on 10/06/2023. A gathering line inside of the tank battery containment which is located 290 feet to the south from the Arnold #2, had failed and crude oil traveled down slope from the tank battery area, aprox. 90 feet away. A neighbor had complained to the pumper, reporting that they smelled gas on Wednesday October 5th or Thursday October 6th. The pumper had looked around and found nothing on those days. On the evening of Friday October 6th crude was discovered inside and outside the containment. Sam Harvey of Bull Run notified the Department of the release on the Arnold lease owned by Armac Resources on Saturday October 7th.The gathering line ran through the dike wall, it is not clear whether the dike wall failed or if the line leaked outside of containment or both. Crude oil is visible outside of containment. When I arrived on site, the area as seen in the photos was already mulched and seeded. I removed several patches of mulch and smelled the soil underneath he mulch, the soil had a strong distinct smell of crude oil. The southwest side of the dike wall has been excavated and the contaminated material was placed inside of a roll off that remains onsite. It is unclear how much if any soil has been removed in the downslope area below the tank battery.There is no evidence of production fluid in the road ditch located along Bauer Hill road. A boom has been placed in the dry ditch as a precaution. I spoke with Sam Harvey and Justin Hansen of Bull Run (who are contract pumping and facilitating the clean up for Armac Resources). I suggested that an underflow dam be placed at the bottom of the area that has been mulched (base of hill), this is to prevent any remaining production fluid from being washed down to the road side ditch of Bauer Hill which leads to an unnamed tributary of Glade Run.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Greylock Prod Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-14
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 877366
Permit API: 059-27910
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Greene Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: On 2/14/20 an incident inspection of the Beacon well pad was conducted in response to a spill (CTS ID: 347983) reported on 2/10/20. The following was observed: >>On 2/11/20 WQSS John Carson spoke with Greylock Representative Keith Eighmey who reported that while drilling using a filming agent foam from an open topped tank blew to the well pad and via a failed seam in the pad containment traveled to the pad's drainage ditches and then to the primary sediment basin and into the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC; unnamed tributary to Frosty Run). The amount of material lost was reported as unknown but minimal. Operator sampling and MSDS were requested. >>At the time of inspection the sediment basin was found to be overflowing via the stand pipe resulting in substantial flow of sediment laden waters bypassing and flowing through site perimeter controls causing accelerated erosion and impact to the WOC. Additionally, the runoff stream and channel off site notably still bore multiple large piles of foam strongly indicating ongoing impact related to the reported spill. At the time of inspection dewatering/pumping out the impacted water from the sediment basin and appropriate disposal of the effluent as site waste was encouraged. Obstruction of the waterway was not approved. This spill and its impact constitutes a violation of 35 P.S. § 6018.301, 35 P.S. § 691.307(a), * 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 91.34(a), 25 Pa. Code § 102.5(m)4, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e), 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1, 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)1, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.53 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. Violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e) and 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1 were related to the failure of site secondary containment and were shown to have been corrected by the operator prior to the time of inspection. >>A concurrent general surface inspection related to the site ESCGP (ESX16-059-0038) was conducted in response to observed site conditions, particularly multiple slope failures.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 1000444
Permit API: 081-21877
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/05/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that at 12:02 am on July 5th, a 5-gallon release of production fluid occurred to the surface of Pad B when a truck was overfilled. Nine wells are staged for production on Pad B. Multiple batteries of frac tanks are present within secondary containment. Adjacent to the frac tank battery near the northwest corner of the pad, an area appeared to have been back-filled with new gravel. No evidence of produced fluid on the pad was observed. Stormwater management features do not appear to have been impacted. The electrical conductivity in the nearest stormwater channel, the north stormwater channel, was 2.12 mS/cm which is consistent with previous inspections. Nine GPUs are present on Pad B within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. The evaporators on Pad B do not appear to be in use any longer. The sump remains installed at the east end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity in the sump was 1872 uS/cm. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Five GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good containment. Violations noted for the release to Pad B and they are considered immediately corrected.
